readerQuestion: How can I use Home Assistant's built-in Schedule helper for several daily settings, including touching blocks that stay on, and verify the routine before it controls a lamp?
directAnswer: Use a UI-created weekly Schedule helper with brightness_pct in each active block and an automation that watches both state and attribute changes. Preview with a persistent notification, then replace only its final action to control an already working dimmable lamp. Keep the enabled toggle accessible; this example applies fixed weekly settings and turns the lamp off in gaps, without automatic sunset, holiday or occupancy rules.
originalContribution: Sections 1 and 4 connect a two-block 70%/25% reading-lamp plan to a six-row expected-outcome rehearsal, including the on-to-on boundary, gap, pause, resume and missing-data case. Section 3 provides a complete notification-only automation with numeric and range guards; section 5 shows the precise action replacement to connect one lamp. The troubleshooting table separates timing, invalid settings, lamp capability and competing-control faults.
limitations: Documentation research and static YAML/Jinja checks only; no live Home Assistant instance, physical lamp, brightness measurements or response-time tests were used. The example does not retry unavailable lamps, enforce settings continuously or provide equipment safety controls. Menu wording can vary by release. The generated cover is an illustration, not a product or installation photograph. Publication, deployment and any subsequent indexing or traffic checks remain the runner's responsibility.

claimChecks.claim: Schedule can be created in Helpers through the UI. Active block Additional data becomes attributes; touching blocks stay on while data changes, and overlapping blocks are rejected. This guide keeps the existing heating guide's thermostat intent separate.
A state trigger with no from, to, not_from or not_to includes attribute-only changes. Adding an empty/null from or to excludes those changes; the article deliberately omits both.
A Home Assistant start trigger can run a new evaluation after startup. The example reads the current plan and does not replay earlier block transitions.
A Toggle helper can supply an explicit pause choice and normally restores its previous state. Pausing this example stops future commands rather than turning the lamp off.
A failed condition inside the action sequence stops subsequent actions. The two guards therefore also apply when the action sequence is run manually.
state_attr returns None when the entity or requested attribute is missing. Missing active-block brightness must not become a zero/off command.

is_number checks conversion to a finite numeric value; the example adds explicit boolean, whole-number and 1-100 range checks. Static template cases include None, unknown, unavailable, empty text, NaN, infinity, booleans, fractions and range boundaries.
The persistent notification is shown in the Home Assistant frontend; reusing notification_id overwrites that message. It is not a phone push alert or a continuing health indicator.

brightness_pct uses percentage values while brightness uses 0-255. The optional action requires an already working dimmable light entity; an on/off smart plug does not establish dimming capability. A turn_on action can update an already-on light.
